newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's regulator says some outside control likely.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's regulator says some outside control likely.

text.p: Lloyd's of London insurance market will almost certainly suggest a move towards some form of external supervision and away from its current self-regulatory status, senior market watchdogs said.

"I would be surprised if the regulatory review does not recommend some sort of external overview," David Gittings, director of Lloyd's regulatory division, told a news conference on market regulation on Monday.
A review group set up in late 1996 to consider market regulation and recommend developments is expected to submit its report by the middle of this year.

Both Gittings and Sir Alan Hardcastle, chairman of Lloyd's regulatory board, said they expected the ruling Council of Lloyd's would eventually become resoponsible to an external regulator, but added that it was too early to say which one.
Lloyd's will continue to enhance its system of regulation, Hardcastle said, but expected further changes after the British election due by early May.

The current ruling Conservative party said in 1995 that it would review Lloyd's regulation in 1997, while the opposition Labour party is expected to carry out a review of all financial services regulation if it forms the next government, he added.
Planned improvements to Lloyd's regulation for the current year include -
-- a consultation paper on the regulation of Lloyd's brokers.
-- new rules for greater protection of capital providers.
The latter follows concerns that there may have been some cases of insider dealing during last year's capacity auctions, Gittings said.
Investigations were under way, he added, but refused to comment on any particular investigation.
Lloyd's also announced the appointment of Noel Lawson as head of regulatory proceedings. His team will prepare and prosecute disciplinary cases in Lloyd's.
Lawson was general counsel and director of exchange supervision at the London Commodity Exchange.
